products.title: The Salt in Her Name
products.description: A debut novel about a woman who returns to a fishing town to bury a mother she barely knew, and stays to untangle a family that would rather she didn’t. Salt-scoured, quietly furious, and tender in the places you don’t expect — the book the whole shop pressed on each other first.
products.seoTitle: The Salt in Her Name by Marisol Vane | Marginalia Books
products.seoDescription: A salt-scoured debut novel about grief, family and a town that keeps its secrets. A Marginalia staff pick.

images.alt: The Salt in Her Name by Marisol Vane

products.title: Tin Ceilings
products.description: Three decades in a shrinking mill town, told through the tenants of one crooked apartment block. Frayne writes ordinary lives with the patience of someone who has actually lived one — funny, unshowy, and by the last chapter, quietly devastating.
products.seoTitle: Tin Ceilings by Odell Frayne | Marginalia Books
products.seoDescription: Three decades of ordinary lives in one crooked apartment block — funny, patient and quietly devastating.

products.title: Small Hours
products.description: Eleven short stories set between midnight and dawn — a night nurse, a locksmith, a woman who can’t stop driving. Belec is a miniaturist of the sleepless hours, and every one of these lands like a held breath. Perfect for readers who think they don’t like short stories.
products.seoTitle: Small Hours by Junia Belec | Marginalia Books
products.seoDescription: Eleven short stories set between midnight and dawn. For readers who think they don’t like short stories.

products.title: A Field Guide to Leaving
products.description: A memoir in the shape of a naturalist’s notebook: every chapter is a species — the swift, the eel, the monarch — and a way of departing. Yao braids migration science with the year they left a marriage and a country, and it is one of the most quietly hopeful books we’ve read in ages.
products.seoTitle: A Field Guide to Leaving by Perrin Yao | Marginalia Books
products.seoDescription: A memoir in the shape of a naturalist’s notebook, braiding migration science with a year of departures.

images.alt: A Field Guide to Leaving by Perrin Yao

products.title: How Cities Breathe
products.description: A clear-eyed, genuinely readable account of what makes a street feel alive — light, width, corners, the humble bench — from an urbanist who’d rather show you than lecture. You’ll never walk your own neighbourhood the same way again. The nonfiction we keep re-ordering.
products.seoTitle: How Cities Breathe by Tomas Ekhart | Marginalia Books
products.seoDescription: A clear, readable account of what makes a street feel alive — light, width, corners, the humble bench.

images.alt: How Cities Breathe by Tomas Ekhart

products.title: Root and Branch
products.description: A year in an old orchard, and a history of the apple that turns out to be a history of us — trade, empire, obsession, and one grafting knife. Calloway is the rare nature writer who is also very funny. Hand it to anyone who thinks they’re not a "nature person".
products.seoTitle: Root and Branch by Neave Calloway | Marginalia Books
products.seoDescription: A year in an old orchard and a history of the apple that turns out to be a history of us.

images.alt: Root and Branch by Neave Calloway

products.title: Marginalia Canvas Tote
products.description: A heavyweight natural-canvas tote screen-printed with our little mark, cut roomy enough for a hardcover and the three paperbacks you didn’t come in for. Made in small runs; flat-bottomed so it stands up on the counter. The bag you’ll actually reach for.
products.seoTitle: Marginalia Canvas Tote — a roomy book bag | Marginalia Books
products.seoDescription: A heavyweight natural-canvas tote, screen-printed and cut roomy enough for a stack of books.

Fiction, nonfiction, or a surprise mix; skip or cancel any time. The gift that keeps someone reading widely all year.
